rationale.High-dose Aspirin / NSAIDs: 650mg aspirin q4-6h. Avoid steroids if possible.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with pleuritic chest pain, fever, malaise, and pericardial friction rub 2-6 weeks after a myocardial infarction. Dressler syndrome is an autoimmune-mediated pericarditis occurring post-MI (or post-cardiac surgery) — immune response to exposed myocardial antigens. ECG: diffuse ST elevation, PR depression (pericarditis pattern). Echo: pericardial effusion (usually small). Differentiate from peri-infarct pericarditis (occurs within days of MI, localized ECG changes over infarct zone, more directly due to transmural necrosis). Treatment: high-dose aspirin (650mg q4-6h) or NSAIDs (ibuprofen). Colchicine added for symptom reduction and recurrence prevention. Avoid steroids unless refractory (impair myocardial healing). NOT heparin (risk of hemorrhagic pericardial effusion/tamponade).
